title: Prison and Drug Rehabilitation Centre Inmates Exercising in Cells
what_it_is: Prison and Drug Rehabilitation Centre Inmates Exercising in Cells

sections.label: Inmate recreational time and exercise
sections.summary: Inmates generally get at least an hour of weekday recreational time for exercise, ball games, television or board games, and may do stretching but not vigorous exercise in cells.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Inmates in the prison or drug rehabilitation centre, generally, have at least an hour of recreational time per day on weekdays.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: They can use this recreational time for physical exercise and ball games in the recreational yard, or other activities, such as watching television and playing board games.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In the cells, inmates are allowed to do stretching exercises, but not vigorous exercise.

sections.label: Cell space and exercise rules
sections.summary: Most cells house four or eight inmates with insufficient space for vigorous exercise, so vigorous in-cell exercise is not allowed even for single occupants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The majority of prison cells are designed to house up to four or eight inmates each, and there is insufficient space for inmates to carry out vigorous exercise without affecting the safety of cellmates, inconveniencing them, or intruding into their personal space.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: To ensure equal treatment, we do not allow vigorous in-cell exercise even if the cell is occupied by only one inmate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Some inmates may claim to be exercising in their cell when shadow-boxing or sparring, or giving tips and teaching others how to fight and attack opponents.
